objectivesInfo.theAFeastForCrowsScenarioIntroducesANewe: <details/>The A Feast for Crows scenario introduces a new way for players to score victory points.<lineBreak/>Players no longer use the Victory track to record the number of Castles and Strongholds they control.<lineBreak2/>Instead, each player now advances on the Victory track by completing the objectives described<lineBreak3/>on his Objective cards, with the goal of being the first and only player to reach position 7.<lineBreak4/><lineBreak5/><details2/>After each Action phase, players resolve these additional steps:<lineBreak6/><details3/><lineBreak7/><details4/>After the Draw Objective Cards step, if any one player occupies position 7 of the Victory track, that player wins the game.<lineBreak8/>If, at this time, two or more players tie by occupying position 7 of the Victory track, the tied player who controls<lineBreak9/>more total land areas wins. If there is still a tie, the tied player who is highest on the Iron Throne Influence track wins.<lineBreak10/><lineBreak11/><details5/><emphasis>Q: When playing A Feast for Crows, what are the tiebreakers at the end of Round 10?</emphasis><lineBreak12/>A: If at the end of Round 10 no player has 7 victory points, the player with the most victory points<lineBreak13/>who is in the highest position on the Iron Throne is the winner.
